newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's TCorp year net profit A$52.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's TCorp year net profit A$52.1 mln.

text.p: New South Wales Treasury Corp (TCorp) said on Thursday it posted a strong performance again in the year to June 30, achieving a net profit of A$52.1 million.
TCorp said it gained A$78 million from its management of state portfolios and its own positions.

"In addition, TCorp repatriated A$90 million of retained earnings to the State Government. This lifted TCorp's contribution to NSW over the 13 years since its establishment to approximately A$2.6 billion," said TCorp Chairman and State Treasury Secretary Michael Lambert.

"TCorp has been successful this year in winning a good share of the available debt management business following the corporatisation of New South wales electricity, ports and other utilities," said Wayne Jarman, TCorp's Chief Executive.

Going forward, Jarman said TCorp would concentrate its efforts on improving the performance of client debt and asset portfolios either directly or through funds management arrangements, as well as providing a commercial return on a capital base of A$30 million.
Following a thorough review of TCorp's capital adequacy requirements, capital for operating purposes has been reduced this year to A$30 million.

Through the A$52.1 million net profit the government received a dividend of A$43.1 million, and along with the retained earnings of A$90 million repatriated in two tranches it provided the State with an aggregate dividend of A$133.1 million after tax, Jarman said.
"Last year was a difficult one for portfolio managers to be confident about market direction," Jarman said.

"We took low risk strategies, maintaining portfolio positions close to neutral most of the time. For the A$20 billion of state debt and financial assets we manage, we outperformed all benchmarks by a modest A$16 million," Jarman added.
